svg.title: Exact factor quotient and internal exchange criterion
svg.desc: For the fixed finite factor N, select a swap-invariant minimal central projection z of the universal normal algebra W. The factor R equals zW. Verify both relative commutants, the nonfactoriality of its two-by-two exchange algebra, and the normal stable ambient isomorphism onto the original M. These conditions give the original normal endomorphism and internal involution.

g.text: Which quotient supplies an actual internal exchange?
Fixed N = L(F∞), with countably many free generators; L = ℓ²ℕ; M = B(L) ⊗̄ N.
Universal normal algebra: W = Π(N ⊗max N)″
Π is the sum of GNS representations of states with two normal marginals.
τ exchanges ι₁(N) and ι₂(N); τ² = id. An exchange automorphism need not be inner.
Choose 0 ≠ z ∈ Z(W), minimal central, with τ(z) = z
R = zW is a factor; A = zι₁(N) ≅ N, B = zι₂(N) ≅ N; A ∨ B = R.
β = τ|R is a normal involution exchanging these two actual copies.
Compute the centre in the specified two-by-two algebra
Cβ = { [ x, y ; β(y), β(x) ] : x,y ∈ R } ⊂ M₂(R)
Cβ is not a factor ⇔ β = Ad s for s = s*, s² = 1R, s ∈ R.
Then w = π(s)v is central; e± = (1 ± w)/2; Cβ ≅ R ⊕ R.
A nontrivial central projection has coefficient y = s/2: it recovers the symmetry.
Also prove both commutants and the whole ambient isomorphism
A′ ∩ R = B, B′ ∩ R = A, Θ : B(L) ⊗̄ B(L) ⊗̄ R → M normally onto.
All these conditions together give σ : M → M and an internal S = S*, S² = 1.
Spatial quotient N ⊗̄ N
The swap exists, but Cβ is a factor.
The internal-exchange test fails.
Type-I quotient in Exercise 6.27
The exchange is internal.
The required ambient Θ cannot exist.
Proofs: Proposition 5I.1 · Lemma 5I.2 · Theorem 5I.3 · Exercises 6.29–6.30.
Source context: Connes, Corollary 11, author PDF44–45; Wiersma, arXiv1506.01671v1, §§2–3.
